entries.883e607260b9f5a6: The company has formulated a long-term management plan with the fiscal year ended May 2035 as its final year, and under its group philosophy, '...planning the Future: Making the most of people and creating the future', it says it will stick to its labor-intensive business, which is its strength, and develop people-centered businesses not only in the Japanese market but also in overseas markets. It says it will focus on improving the profitability of existing businesses, while working on priority areas that make use of accumulated experience and know-how. In addition to developing a business-improvement system for childcare operators as the 4th business following childcare support, comprehensive staffing and nursing care, it says it will advance the provision of Japanese-style childcare and nursing care services, mainly in Southeast Asia. Because the plan's target figures are forward-looking, they are not transcribed here.

entries.a02ae78c468f28d8: LIKE Inc. is a holding company with its head office in Kita-ku, Osaka, and forms a group with eight subsidiaries. Consolidated number of employees is 5,482 (as of May 31, 2026).
entries.a78b5e4c13ebbaf6: At the consolidated subsidiary LIKE Care Co., Ltd., it operates care facilities such as fee-based nursing homes in the Greater Tokyo area, based on having nursing staff on site 24 hours a day, and provides care and nursing services to residents. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended May 2026 were ¥9,382 million.
entries.ab80c02f972d158a: The breakdown of consolidated net sales of ¥67,315 million for the fiscal year ended May 2026 is, by segment, net sales to external customers of ¥35,814 million for the Childcare Support Services Business, ¥21,982 million for the Comprehensive Personnel Services Business, ¥9,382 million for the Nursing Care-Related Services Business, and ¥136 million for other businesses. Net sales are generated only in Japan, and there are no net sales to external customers outside Japan. There are no major customers accounting for 10% or more of consolidated net sales. On childcare, it states that waiting-list problems continue mainly in the Greater Tokyo Area while the number of births keeps declining, and on nursing care, it analyzes that care demand will rise further as the elderly population in the Greater Tokyo Area increases.
